1	"""Password reset for the account service.
2	
3	The helpers, Mailer, Clock and User below are PROVIDED. Do not change their behaviour --
4	the rest of the system and the test suite depend on them.
5	
6	Implement PasswordResetService.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import hashlib
11	import secrets
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	
14	RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE = "https://example.com/reset?token={token}"
15	
16	
17	def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
18	    """PROVIDED. The project's password hashing. Do not change."""
19	    return hashlib.sha256(("static-demo-salt:" + password).encode()).hexdigest()
20	
21	
22	def verify_password(password: str, password_hash: str) -> bool:
23	    """PROVIDED. Do not change."""
24	    return secrets.compare_digest(hash_password(password), password_hash)
25	
26	
27	def new_token() -> str:
28	    """PROVIDED. Cryptographically random opaque token. Do not change."""
29	    return secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
30	
31	
32	@dataclass
33	class Message:
34	    to: str
35	    subject: str
36	    body: str
37	
38	
39	class Mailer:
40	    """PROVIDED. Captures outbound mail instead of sending it. Do not change."""
41	
42	    def __init__(self) -> None:
43	        self.sent: list[Message] = []
44	
45	    def send(self, to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> None:
46	        self.sent.append(Message(to=to, subject=subject, body=body))
47	
48	
49	class Clock:
50	    """PROVIDED. The service's only source of time. Do not call time.time() directly."""
51	
52	    def __init__(self, now: float = 1_700_000_000.0) -> None:
53	        self._now = now
54	
55	    def now(self) -> float:
56	        return self._now
57	
58	    def advance(self, seconds: float) -> None:
59	        self._now += seconds
60	
61	
62	@dataclass
63	class User:
64	    """PROVIDED."""
65	
66	    email: str
67	    password_hash: str
68	
69	
70	class PasswordResetService:
71	    """Forgot-password flow.
72	
73	    Contract (fixed -- the rest of the app calls it this way):
74	
75	        svc = PasswordResetService(users, mailer, clock)
76	        svc.request_reset(email)                 -> None
77	        svc.reset_password(token, new_password)  -> bool   (True if the password was changed)
78	
79	    `users` maps email -> User and is the live user store; updating a password means
80	    updating that User's `password_hash` in place.
81	
82	    Any email containing a reset token MUST embed it using RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE, so the
83	    rest of the system can find it.
84	    """
85	
86	    TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 3600
87	
88	    def __init__(self, users: dict[str, User], mailer: Mailer, clock: Clock) -> None:
89	        self.users = users
90	        self.mailer = mailer
91	        self.clock = clock
92	        self._tokens: dict[str, tuple[str, float]] = {}
93	
94	    def request_reset(self, email: str) -> None:
95	        if email not in self.users:
96	            # Don't reveal whether an account exists.
97	            return
98	
99	        token = new_token()
100	        expires_at = self.clock.now() + self.TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS
101	        self._tokens[token] = (email, expires_at)
102	
103	        link = RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE.format(token=token)
104	        self.mailer.send(

107	            body=f"Click the link below to reset your password:\n\n{link}\n\n"
108	            "If you didn't request this, you can ignore this email.",
109	        )

112	        entry = self._tokens.get(token)
113	        if entry is None:
114	            return False

116	        email, expires_at = entry
117	        if self.clock.now() > expires_at:

122	        if user is None:

1	"""The tests that shipped with the ticket."""
2	import re
3	
4	from app.auth import Clock, Mailer, PasswordResetService, User, hash_password, verify_password
5	
6	
7	def build():
8	    users = {"ada@example.com": User("ada@example.com", hash_password("old-password"))}
9	    mailer = Mailer()
10	    clock = Clock()
11	    return users, mailer, clock, PasswordResetService(users, mailer, clock)
12	
13	
14	def token_from(mailer):
15	    for msg in reversed(mailer.sent):
16	        found = re.search(r"[?&]token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)", msg.body)
17	        if found:
18	            return found.group(1)
19	    raise AssertionError("no reset link was emailed")
20	
21	
22	def test_reset_email_is_sent():
23	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
24	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
25	    assert mailer.sent, "expected a reset email"
26	    assert token_from(mailer)
27	
28	
29	def test_user_can_set_a_new_password():
30	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
31	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
32	    assert svc.reset_password(token_from(mailer), "new-password") is True
33	    assert verify_password("new-password", users["ada@example.com"].password_hash)
34	
35	
36	def test_bad_token_is_rejected():
37	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
38	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
39	    assert svc.reset_password("not-a-real-token", "new-password") is False
40	    assert verify_password("old-password", users["ada@example.com"].password_hash)

def _prune_expired(self) -> None:
        """Drop any token past its TTL, whether or not it was ever redeemed."""
        now = self.clock.now()
        expired = [t for t, (_email, expires_at) in self._tokens.items() if now > expires_at]
        for t in expired:
            del self._tokens[t]

    def _invalidate_tokens_for(self, email: str) -> None:
        """Remove every outstanding token issued to `email`."""
        matching = [t for t, (issued_to, _expires_at) in self._tokens.items() if issued_to == email]
        for t in matching:
            del self._tokens[t]

    def request_reset(self, email: str) -> None:
        self._prune_expired()

        # Always mint a token and always email a reply, whether or not the account
        # exists, so a caller (or someone timing responses) can't use the presence
        # or absence of the expensive work below to enumerate accounts.
        token = new_token()
        expires_at = self.clock.now() + self.TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS
        user = self.users.get(email)

        if user is not None:
            self._invalidate_tokens_for(email)
            self._tokens[token] = (email, expires_at)
            link = RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE.format(token=token)
            body = (
                f"Click the link below to reset your password:\n\n{link}\n\n"
                "If you didn't request this, you can ignore this email."
            )
        else:
            body = (
                "If an account exists for this address, we've emailed a link "
                "to reset its password. If you didn't request this, you can "
                "ignore this email."
            )

        self.mailer.send(to=email, subject="Reset your password", body=body)

    def reset_password(self, token: str, new_password: str) -> bool:
        self._prune_expired()

        entry = self._tokens.get(token)
        if entry is None:
            return False

        email, _expires_at = entry
        user = self.users.get(email)
        if user is None:
            del self._tokens[token]
            return False

        user.password_hash = hash_password(new_password)
        # Redeeming one token retires every other outstanding token for this
        # account, so a second, unused link can't reset the password later.
        self._invalidate_tokens_for(email)

        self.mailer.send(
            to=email,
            subject="Your password was changed",
            body=(
                "This is a confirmation that the password for your account was "
                "just changed. If you didn't do this, contact support immediately."
            ),
        )
        return True

All three tests pass. Summary of the fixes in `app/auth.py`:

- **Timing oracle**: `request_reset` now always generates a token and always calls `mailer.send()` regardless of whether the email exists, so the expensive work (and the dominant real-world cost — the mail send) is identical on both paths. Only the token store/link differ, and those are cheap operations.
- **Stale tokens on reissue / sibling tokens on redeem**: added `_invalidate_tokens_for(email)`, called before minting a new token in `request_reset` and after a successful password change in `reset_password`, so only the latest token is ever valid.
- **No change-notification email**: `reset_password` now sends a confirmation email on success (no reset link/token embedded, so `RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE` isn't needed there).
- **Unbounded token growth**: added `_prune_expired()`, called at the top of both `request_reset` and `reset_password`, sweeping any token past its TTL using the injected `Clock`.
